items.title: From blunt to precision: Engineering microbiome therapeutics against cancer.
items.one_liner: Two recent papers in Cell Host & Microbe move microbiome therapeutics beyond selecting "beneficial" strains. By turning bacterial surfaces into oral vaccine couriers and resident microbial metabolism into a controllable reactor, they show how location, control, and measurable output can transform the gut into a precision platform for cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: A microbial signal rewires the adipose-ovary dialogue.
items.one_liner: In this issue of Cell Host & Microbe, Chen et al. show that a gut microbial metabolite reprograms adipose ceramide metabolism to influence ovarian function. By placing adipose tissue between microbial and reproductive signaling, the study reveals how inter-organ communication couples the metabolic and ovarian dimensions of polycystic ovary syndrome.
